key_insight: A dynamically transforming 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) additive couples crystallization control with interface passivation in lead-free tin-based perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: This molecular engineering approach targets both film formation and interfacial defects to improve photovoltaic efficiency and operational stability.
method: Coordinate PX carbonyl groups with Sn²⁺ to stabilize precursor complexes and regulate crystal growth.
Anneal films to induce PX transformation, suggested to produce amidinium-functionalized species.
Passivate surface A-site vacancies to suppress nonradiative recombination.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 15.18% power conversion efficiency and retention of 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 hours of continuous illumination.
watch_item: The proposed amidinium-forming transformation remains tentative, and the abstract does not specify illumination-test conditions or device-scale reproducibility.
paper_title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
